A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete paper, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 2–10 and 13–22 are identical; differences on the remaining pages are fully readable.

before.justification: v6 reports original simulations and trained-network spectral measurements on synthetic manifolds, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA in Sections 7–8 and the appendices.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including the nonlinear-manifold experiment in Appendix D and per-image spectral analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The diffusion models, training procedures, and spectral estimation methods are unchanged, including the orthogonalized perturbations and central-difference procedure in Appendix C, Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic linear manifolds, nonlinear ellipsoid scenario in Appendix D, and MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA datasets. No task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The analytical-versus-learned comparisons in Figure 4 and the comparison against Stanczuk et al. (2022)'s standard SVD procedure in Figure 9 are identical. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendices B–C retain the same model configurations, training budgets, sample counts, perturbation procedures, and singular-value normalization settings.

E4.justification: The variance and subspace analyses in Figure 3, spectral-estimation comparison in Figure 9, nonlinear-manifold analysis in Appendix D, and per-image analyses in Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 7 retain the same reporting of numerical spectra collected over 100 realizations of F. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes elsewhere.

E6.justification: All result plots and associated findings are identical, including the spectral-gap dynamics, analytical-versus-learned spectra, and additional results in Figures 9–13. No numerical correction or result entry is added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, spectral-gap formulas, and derivations in Sections 2–6 and Appendices A and D are identical, including the replica-method analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions: random-matrix analysis of diffusion geometry, three generative phases, and an explanation of avoiding manifold overfitting.

C2.justification: The explanations of the three phases, qualifications concerning linear manifolds, discussion of discrepancies between theory and learned spectra, and applicability arguments in Appendix D are unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, data quantities, GPU information, and spectral computation instructions in Table 1 and Appendices B–C are identical. The affiliation and acknowledgment additions provide no new technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 9 and the cited-work set are unchanged. The Sakamoto et al. (2024) reference moves from page 11 to page 12 without any bibliographic or positioning change.

P1.justification: v7 adds Gianluigi Silvestri's OnePlanet Research Center affiliation and an acknowledgment of support from the Province of Gelderland, and rephrases the equal-contribution note. Scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v7 reformats the author block, moves the equal-contribution statement to a footnote, and reflows the acknowledgments and references across pages 11–12. All scientific figures, tables, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v7 updates institutional attribution and funding credit and makes modest layout adjustments. These administrative changes leave scientific clarity, theoretical support, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and all appendices unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
